subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should maintainers repair/adopt the linked SSRF socket-error PR as the fix path, or choose a different guarded-fetch dispatcher repair before closing this issue?
rationale: The remaining work changes the SSRF network security boundary and the current linked PR has identified proof and proxy-pinning blockers, so automation should not create a second fix or treat this as solved without maintainer direction.

options.title: Repair the linked PR
options.body: Keep this issue open and require the linked PR to preserve explicit-proxy DNS pinning while adding real IPv6-unreachable proof before merge.

options.title: Replace with a narrower maintainer fix
options.body: Close or supersede the linked PR only after a maintainer-owned branch proves the same crash path without weakening SSRF pinning.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Leave both items paused until maintainers get Docker or Crabbox proof of the current crash path and then choose the implementation shape.

recommendation.title: Repair the linked PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require the linked PR to preserve explicit-proxy DNS pinning while adding real IPv6-unreachable proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The best available history signal ties this security-boundary choice to prior explicit-proxy SSRF pinning work.
